data.rationale: Tile the query-sequence dimension i with block size 64. For S=256, D=64, this creates 4 query tiles. A tile of 64 rows × 64 head-dim fits the Q block in ~32 KB of SMEM (64×64×fp16=8 KB) while enabling the online-softmax running max/sum registers to stay live. 64 is the canonical FlashAttention Br block size balancing SMEM vs register pressure.

Tile the key/value-sequence dimension j with block size 64 (Bc=64). This is the inner loop over KV chunks in flash-attention. 64×64 K tile (8 KB fp16) + 64×64 V tile (8 KB fp16) + 64×64 Q tile (8 KB fp16) = 24 KB total, well within the 49 KB SMEM budget. Larger j tiles reduce global memory round-trips for the softmax denominator.
Map batch dimension b to threadblock.y. With B=1 this doesn't add parallelism yet but correctly sets up the 2D threadblock grid needed for the b×h → SM mapping.

Map the head dimension h to threadblock.x. With H=8 this creates 8 independent threadblocks across the 30 SMs, each processing one full attention head. Combined with 4 query tiles from the i=64 tiling, we get 8×4=32 threadblock launches — nearly perfectly filling 30 SMs. This is the primary source of GPU parallelism for this problem size.

Stage the Q tile in registers. For the 64-row Q tile, keeping the D=64 head dimension row-slice in registers avoids repeated global memory reads during the inner j-loop over KV tiles. This is the standard FlashAttention optimization where Q rows remain resident across all KV chunk iterations.

Stage K tile in registers. The K block (64×64 fp16) will be loaded once per j-tile and held in registers/SMEM during the QK^T matmul. Placing in registers reduces SMEM pressure and latency for the inner D-dimension reduction.

Stage V tile in registers. V (64×64 fp16) is loaded per j-tile and used in the final weighted sum O += softmax_weights @ V. Keeping it in registers means no extra SMEM round-trip for the output accumulation phase and enables direct FMA pipelining.

Map the tiled i (query-row) dimension to warps within each threadblock. With i-tile=64 rows and 32 threads/warp, each warp handles 2 query rows. This distributes the Q@K^T and weighted-sum-V work across warps within the block, enabling warp-level parallelism for the online softmax accumulation loop.
